name: Gilbert O'Sullivan
hook: An Irish singer-songwriter whose refusal to license a sample, and the court case that followed, changed how hip-hop was made.

blurb.age7: An Irish singer. He took Biz Markie to court for using his song without permission, and won.
blurb.age13: Raymond 'Gilbert' O'Sullivan was born in Waterford, Ireland, in 1946 and grew up in Swindon, England. His 1972 song 'Alone Again (Naturally)' was number one in America for six weeks. In 1991 Biz Markie used a loop of its piano on his song 'Alone Again'. Biz had asked O'Sullivan's permission and been refused, and the record came out anyway. O'Sullivan sued and won, and from then on anyone sampling a record had to get permission first.
blurb.adult: O'Sullivan's place on the map is entirely the lawsuit: Grand Upright Music v. Warner Bros. Records (1991). His objection was to his song being used without consent, and the court agreed that unlicensed sampling was infringement. The ruling made him, a pop singer-songwriter far from hip-hop, one of the people who most changed how hip-hop records were made.
